summary: PUMA melanoma tissue-class contract with epidermis-specific semantics, separate nuclei annotations, primary/metastatic conditioning, and immutable white background.

annotation_traits: tissue and nuclei annotations are separate annotation layers
the canonical Normal epithelium label specifically means epidermis in this profile
ROIs include primary and metastatic melanoma and must be stratified by source
semantic_limitations: Normal epithelium means epidermis, not a generic normal epithelial compartment.
Immune cells are available in the nuclei layer but there is no immune tissue-region label in the profile.
Other tissue is not encoded; unmodeled tissue must not be invented from background.

rules.claim: Require primary-versus-metastatic status and source site, and retrieve statistics/examples from the matching stratum.
rules.required_observation: Validate case provenance before loading empirical thresholds or reference panels.
exceptions: Use a reviewed hierarchical fallback only when a stratum has insufficient samples and report the uncertainty.
counterexamples: Applying epidermal-interface priors from primary cutaneous melanoma to a lymph-node metastasis.
Comparing component size without stratifying source site.
expected_morphology: Reference examples share the relevant primary/metastatic tissue context.
forbidden_morphology: Epidermis-dependent reasoning in a metastatic ROI lacking epidermis.
known_limitations: The current profile has no certified stratified statistics artifact.

rules.claim: Preserve white background exactly and never use it as tumor, stroma, epidermis, necrosis, or vessel source/target support.
rules.required_observation: Verify zero/background pixels remain identical and no selected scene component is background.
counterexamples: Expanding dermal tumor into blank slide background.
Filling a white cleft to connect two tumor regions.
forbidden_morphology: Background seeding, filling, crossing, or bridging.
known_limitations: Tears and processing clefts may look white on H&E; the mask contract remains pixel-preserving.

rules.claim: Interpret canonical Normal epithelium strictly as epidermis and preserve its layered continuity unless an epidermis-specific primitive is requested.
rules.required_observation: Trace the epidermal band on the source mask and H&E and determine whether the case is primary cutaneous tissue or a metastatic site.
exceptions: A reviewed epidermal invasion or ulceration primitive.
counterexamples: Treating epidermis as generic glandular normal epithelium.
Cutting an isolated notch into intact epidermis during dermal tumor growth.
expected_morphology: An intact, continuous epidermal band remains unchanged in a generic burden edit.
forbidden_morphology: Remote epidermal deletion, split, island, or false ulceration.
known_limitations: The tissue label alone does not encode epidermal layers or ulceration criteria.

rules.claim: Do not synthesize an immune tissue-region mask from the nuclei layer or from Stroma; PUMA immune information belongs to separate cell annotations.
rules.required_observation: Check whether the requested primitive requires a tissue-region label absent from the profile and reject it before planning.
exceptions: A separately designed cell-edit workflow may operate on the nuclei layer without mutating tissue semantics.
counterexamples: Converting stromal pixels to Immune infiltrate because lymphocytes are present.
Rasterizing immune nuclei into a solid immune tissue component.
forbidden_morphology: Invented immune tissue regions in the semantic mask.
known_limitations: Cell-level editing is outside phase3_mask_edit_refine v1.

rules.claim: Do not create tumor islands, merge separated tumor foci, fill necrotic holes, split epidermis, or absorb vessels during a generic burden edit.
rules.required_observation: Compare source/target connected components and holes and preserve every non-source label exactly.
exceptions: A dedicated perivascular, epidermal-invasion, ulceration, or necrosis primitive with its own contract.
counterexamples: A tumor bridge across stroma joining separate foci.
Tumor expansion that closes a labeled necrotic center.
Tumor growth that swallows a small vessel component.
expected_morphology: One selected interface is deformed while unrelated epidermis, vessel, necrosis, and tumor components remain intact.
forbidden_morphology: New islands, merges, splits, filled holes, or unrequested label loss.
known_limitations: Microscopic satellite detection requires sufficient resolution and expert review.
